title: Gaussian polynomial features: actual L² means and ambient gradients
source_anchor: Complete source-only.json: A1-A4, D1-D6, C1-C7 and T1-T6.
target_statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\), and let \(S=\{w\in E:\|w\|=1\}\). Let \(P\) be a probability measure on \(E\times\mathbb R\) whose first marginal is \(\gamma\). Fix a real polynomial \(p\), and assume the actual response \((x,y)\mapsto y\) belongs to \(H=L^2(P;\mathbb R)\). Define the literal feature and directional derivative by \(f_w(x,y)=p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) and \(df_{w,v}(x,y)=p^{\prime}(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle v,x\rangle\). All these functions belong to \(H\). There exist one family of continuous linear maps \(D(w):E\to H\) and positive constants \(M_1,M_2\), chosen before every parameter law and every subsequent evaluation point, with the following properties. Writing \(F(w)=[f_w]\), we have \(D(w)v=[df_{w,v}]\) and \(F\) has Fréchet derivative \(D(w)\) at every ambient \(w\). The displayed operator bounds hold on the closed unit ball. For every probability \(\rho\) on \(S\), all scalar sections defining the predictor are integrable, \(F|_S\) is Bochner integrable, and the predictor composed with the first-coordinate map belongs to \(H\), with class equal to its Bochner mean \(m_\rho\). The literal scalar potential has an integrable defining integrand at every ambient \(w\); it equals \(2\langle m_\rho-\ell,F(w)\rangle_H\) and has actual ambient gradient \(2D(w)^*(m_\rho-\ell)\) there. On the unit sphere, subtracting the normal component gives the final displayed projection formula. The same \(D,M_1,M_2\) is used throughout.
